The power is in the future, so is the responsibility.
debates.synthesis: Environmental ethics questions the notion of man as a king apart from nature. Future generations, non-human life forms, local communities, and the need for scientific evidence and development must all be placed in the same rational framework. The ecological formula of parallel philosophy is the convenience of today rather than the survival of the future.
debates.source: Gajendra Thakur's Parallel Philosophy · Modernity, science and responsibility · Chapter 64

debates.objection: Multidimensionality does not become relativism after all
debates.proof: The first basic tenet of the parallel philosophy proposed in this text is that of multidimensional rationalism. This does not mean that all evidence is the same or that all beliefs can be true. It means that there is truth and knowledge is possible, but knowledge is not the only kind of evidence. Direct estimates, reliable statements, documents, historical sources, scientific experiments, self-experience, statistical data, and institutional records are their respective domains of reference. Accept the multiplicity of evidence, not the chaos of evidence. The human question is not a uniform one. The way to know the effects of medicines is different from personal religious experience. the way to know the dates of ancient dynasties is different from laboratory-testing. the way to know the experiences of personal suffering is different from census-tables. Evidence that is reasonable in one area may be insufficient in another. Multiplicity takes into account these regional differences. The evidence is overwhelming, but the decision requires testing. Prudence means that the claims made should be clear, the evidence should relate to the claim, the contrary evidence should be heard, the credibility of the sources should be checked, the conclusions should be limited by the strength of the evidence, and revisions should be possible when new evidence emerges. This is not infallibility; it is disciplined error correction. Direct perception is a strong source of immediate experience, but confusion is possible. Inferences range from the known to the unknown, but require scope or causality. Words or testimonies are the basis of vast social knowledge, but the credibility of the speaker, institution, and source must be tested. Documentation is evidence of history, but construction - intent and silence are to be seen. Scientific testing is one of the best public practices in empirical questions of nature, but ethical values do not emanate from the laboratory itself. Self-realization may be meaningful evidence of private life, but not an automatically sufficient basis for universal public claims. Personal religious experiences can be a deep foundation of faith for individuals. But we felt that this was not a public enough reason to impose the law on other citizens. In this way, private evidence is not compromised; its scope is clear. The same principle applies in other areas: individual success does not prove economic policy. a patient 's experience does not prove the universal effect of medicine. a record does not prove the whole history. Multidimensional rationalism does not make science always superior, folklore always inferior, or vice versa. The question is the nature of the claim. Folklore is important for the study of what communities consider sacred, as instrumental data for weather temperatures are more accurate than folktales. Contemporary inscriptions to ancient events may be a more direct historical source than later legends. The value of the proof is context-specific, and the truth is not arbitrary. Nyaya, Mīmāṃsā, Buddhist and other Indian traditions debate at length the number, nature, and authenticity of the Puranas. Multidimensional rationalism draws inspiration from these traditions, particularly by making knowledge-sources the subject of analysis rather than the repetition of a single classical school. Modern science, historiography, sociology, and digital source-review are also included in this framework. Empiricism shows the importance of experience, rationalism shows the structure of reasoning, pragmatism results in inquiry, social epistemology shows the role of testimony and agency, and modern fallibilism shows the importance of revisionism. Parallel philosophy does not make a closed synthesis of these insights; it communicates them problem by problem. If everyone said we needed evidence and there was no common standard, then public knowledge would be fragmented. Medical tests and rumors, records and fiction, expert statistics and made-up numbers are not on the same level. Plurality is not the same thing as equality. There are many types of proof, but the claim-proof relationship will be worthy of public criticism.
debates.response: No, because the types of evidence are considered to be numerous and the standard of truth is not exhaustive. Each claim must bear reasonable area proof, rationale, counterarguments, and amendments. The formula is: Accept plurality of evidence, not chaos of evidence.
debates.synthesis: Multidimensional rationalism is the epistemological basis of parallel philosophy. It rejects on the one hand the imperialism of a single system of evidence; on the other hand, the anarchy of all these equal sources. Truth is to be found in objective evidence, shared criticism, source-review, epistemic humility, and revisionism.
debates.source: Gajendra Thakur's Parallel Philosophy · Parallel Philosophy: constructive theses · Chapter 65

debates.proof: Another theory is that of coexistential realism. It starts with a rejection of the two extremes. Firstly, the world is only a construction of our consciousness or language; secondly, reality is only a lifeless mass of separate objects and not of any fundamental importance to relationships. Parallel philosophy says that the universe resists, independent of our will, but we always experience it through relationships, body language, history, and social position. The fire does not depend on my opinion of whether it will burn or not: disease, flood, gravity, hunger, bodily harm, the weight of things, all resist outside our choice of reality. This is why coexistential realism is not relativism. There is a difference between what we think it looks like and what it really is. The need for proof, testing and improvement stems from this. But it is incomplete to consider matter only as a solitary substance. Man exists at the same time in relation to his son, mother, citizen, worker, linguistic person, friend, neighbour, biological organism and historical heir. Society is not just a collection of individuals; institutions, rules, language, memory and authority structure relationships. Rivers are not just bodies of water; they are also relationships of ecology, agriculture, geography, memory, and livelihood. Coexistential realism accepts the independent dignity of the individual but does not consider them to be self-sufficient atoms imagined outside society. Individuals develop through language, upbringing, education, resources, and institutions. However, society does not have total power over the individual. Relationships make people, and people can change relationships. In this duality, both freedom and responsibility take place. The same reality may be experienced differently in different social spaces. Disaster-statistics for flood authorities may include crop failures for farmers, school breakdowns for children, and displacement for migrant families. These multiple experiences do not make reality arbitrary but rather show its multilayeredness. The material phenomena are one, their human relations are many. Constructive dialogue is possible through the materialistic tendencies of Nyaya-Vaisheshika, the relational-sensitivities of Buddhist phenomenology, the multifacetedness of the Jaina Encyclopedia, Aristotle 's social man, Hegel 's critique of belief, and contemporary relational philosophy. But the theory of this text is not a repetition of any one tradition; it is an independent answer to the question of how to put objectivity and relational experience together. The objection is that if every knowledge is built into social relations, then truth will become a plaything of entities or attitudes. Incidents often occur not for one reason but through a web of conditions. Rainfall in floods, river courses, dams, settlements, and warnings are combined. The main reason why questions can change according to the purpose is the scientific explanation, the legal fault or the prevention. Multifactoriality should not obscure the responsibility. The role of the agent who could have controlled the known risk should be distinguished. Looking at relationships is not an infinite list. It is necessary to separate out the substantial contributors and the background conditions. Ability is not just a quality inside the body. The mobility of wheelchair users is combined with roads, buildings and transport. The social consequences of incompetence can change when the environment changes. This view did not deny the reality of the body. Medical and accessible environments are different and complementary measures. Treating a person as the only object of correction is unfair. The policy will add technical standards and resources to the affected person 's experience. The universal design allows for more people to have abilities. Not all relationships need to be saved. Respect can be protected by leaving a violent family, exploitative work, or oppressive community. Coexistence would have become bondage without the right to exit. Exit decisions can leave real liabilities to others, such as debt or shared resources. There should be a safe separation of responsibilities.
debates.response: Related to knowledge and object resistance. The knower is related.Truth is not just a desire for connection. My description may be influenced by language and perspective, but Jagat thwarts the misrepresentation. Medicine, engineering, agriculture, and history define the limits of true resistance in science. Relativism, therefore, refers to a state of knowledge and not to the arbitrariness of truth.
debates.synthesis: Coexistential realism holds that reality is independent of our will, but its human experience is reduced to a web of relationships. The person is real, the society is real, the body is real, the meaning is real, the object is real, and the relationship is real. This theory posits an alternative to both rigid individualism and rigid collectivism.
debates.source: Gajendra Thakur's Parallel Philosophy · Parallel Philosophy: constructive theses · Chapter 66

debates.proof: The moral center of Parallel Philosophy is dignity. Dignity means that the basic moral values of every human being precede birth, caste, sex, wealth, language, religion, ability, position, utility or acceptance by the majority. Man cannot be seen merely as a carrier of means, numbers, labour power, voters, consumers or community prestige. Dignity is a claim to equal human status. This claim does not say that all individuals have the same qualities, needs, and accomplishments or responsibilities. It says that no one is inferior in basic human qualities. Criminals should also get due process.poor should also get respect.minorities should also get equal citizenship.dissidents should also be treated without disrespect. Ethical superiority based on caste, race, gender, or family is inconsistent with this principle. Birth is a coincidence, not an achievement. Birthright privilege seeks public justification when it is transformed into state, education, property, representation, or social opportunity. Dignity-based ethics propose four main criteria: Does an action cause unnecessary suffering? What constitutes an unreasonable loss of autonomy? Does it deny that someone is of the same human quality? Are the benefits and burdens fairly distributed? These four questions examine policy, family behaviour, medicine, technology, punishment and social practice. Individuals make independent decisions meaningfully when they have access to information, options, minimal resources, and protection from pressure. The choice between starvation, racial fear, economic dependence, or domestic violence may be mistaken for complete freedom. Dignity therefore demands an examination of the actual circumstances, with formal acknowledgment. The language of authority alone sometimes undermines the morality of the relationship; compassion alone can sometimes become a patriarchal preserve. Parallel philosophy adds equality of rights and humanity of compassion. Compassion does not allow control of the individual. authority does not insensitivity. Kant 's doctrine of not treating human beings as mere means, Buddhist compassion, Jain non-violence and Ambedkar 's insistence on equality, freedom, and fraternity communicate this framework. But the dignity-based morality has its own independent structure in this text: equal status, autonomy, suffering-minority and just burden-sharing. The objection is that the term can be used by all parties at their own convenience. Dignity in severe disease is linked not only to the biological duration of life but also to pain-control, cognition, relationships, and the value of the individual. It is not necessary to respect every possibility of treatment. The decision to end a life is complex, requiring capacity, pressure, treatment options, and legal protections. Due to financial burdens, the weaker person may not consider themselves burdened and make decisions. Telling the truth in end-care is not without compassion; the language, the timing and the precise form of hope are crucial. Stay in the patient 's health centre if family and patient preferences clash. Freedom may be limited upon conviction, but torture or degrading treatment is not. The punishment is on the deed and not on the humanity. Prison conditions should not become an undeclared extension of a judicial sentence. Monitoring, complaints, and rehabilitation are essential. The dignity of the victim is also central. The discussion of the rights of criminals should not drown out the voices of victims; it should be a combination of retribution, protection and truth-acceptance. Four questions can be asked whether the policy assumes dignity: The person was heard The reason has been explained. It is possible to make an appeal. The minimum condition of life is safe. Decisions can be arbitrary with respectful language, while abusive procedures can lead to harm if the outcome is good. Both the process and the result should be checked. Dignity-assessment requires evidence of the person affected but also comparative data. A shining example can hide the institutional pattern.
debates.response: Turn Dignity into a Testable Moral Question Dignity is not just a sentimental word, so in this chapter, it is governed by four criteria: suffering, autonomy, equal status, and fair distribution. If a practice consistently fails in all four of these, its moral justification is seriously undermined.
debates.synthesis: Parallelism says we can claim our dignity coherently only when we assume the same dignity as others. Morality is the rule of mutual respect, not just the defence of one 's honour.
debates.source: Gajendra Thakur's Parallel Philosophy · Parallel Philosophy: constructive theses · Chapter 67

debates.proof: Democracy cannot be abolished by elections alone, nor by the institution of parliament or capital. The political doctrine of the Parallel Philosophy is multicentric democracy. This implies a possible decentralization of power, knowledge, resources, and decision-making but equal constitutional protection of fundamental rights. Bringing decisions that directly affect people 's lives closer to those affected as much as possible can increase accountability. Rural and urban areas, states and union territories ask different questions at different levels. Not every problem will ask for the same solution to the remote center. Local power can also become a means of caste, gender, wealth or majority domination. The other half of a multicentric democracy is therefore necessarily one of fundamental rights, equal citizenship, judicial protection and a higher structure of appeals. Local autonomy is not above all human rights. Majority is a method of judging and not proof of truth. In democracies, opposition, free press, judiciary, freedom of association, information-access and peaceful dissent define the limits of majority. Winning elections does not give the state unfettered control over all institutions. Political decentralization is simply not enough. Knowledge is unequal when universities, languages, publications, media, archives and cultural institutions are confined to a single centre. Multicentric democracies value the development of regional languages, local expertise, and diverse institutional centres as democratic values. Too much private economic concentration can also affect democracy. The question of the responsibility of an institution that exerts unusual control over public discourse, employment, information or resources may be of state-level importance. Multicentrism does not see power as only government. Federalism may be a form of polycentrism, but the theory is broader than that. The fundamental question is at what level can a decision be taken with the greatest knowledge, responsibility, participation and rights-protection. The answer to this question may vary depending on the topic. The objection is that too much central decision-making can lead to inequality and fragmentation. The metropolis would concentrate employment, universities, and capital; the surrounding area would provide labor, water, and food. Administrative boundaries do not capture the actual dependencies. The cost of development of the centre may be borne by the external sector. The multicentre plan calls for a common agency for transport, housing, environment and revenue. However, the regional coordination did not make the local body nominal. Look at the representative population as well as the voice of affected resources. The decision data should be available in the local language. Adding centralized data services can reduce fraud, but a single error can prevent many rights. Mass surveillance can become a force for political abuse. Purpose-boundary, minimal data and localized improvements and independent oversight are required. Citizens will know who has access and how to correct incorrect records. Decentralized copy does not automatically protect privacy; local abuse is possible. Laws and accountability are needed along with technical frameworks. A separate local entity can test the new policy. Success is about sharing experiences and learning from failures. This has the benefit of reducing the risk of large scale homogeneous experiments. But civil liberties are not an object of experimentation. Testing should be informed, timely, and measurable; not just risking vulnerable areas. General indicators are needed for comparison, as well as the location of local targets. Imitation is by looking at the context. Delays in seeking consent at multiple levels can lead to duplication and confusion of responsibilities. A crisis or infrastructure needs a clear center. The answer is not complete fragmentation but role-splitting. It should be clear from the beginning what level will constitute a standard, what is applicable, and what is appealed. The shared digital information can increase coordination. Speed is not the only value. The costs of a quick bad decision can be high. The timing of the decision should be dictated by the risk.
debates.response: Multicentricity is not fragmentation; it is layered responsibility. Subjects such as national defence, currency, comprehensive rights-security, and interstate co-ordination may ask for centres; local water, school culture or town-planning may ask for local roles. The doctrine is not anti-centrism but unnecessary anti-centrism.
debates.synthesis: The essence of a multicentric democracy is sovereignty where necessary, and authority and transparency and accountability at every level. Democracy is not just a form of governance; it is the moral discipline of power-sharing.
debates.source: Gajendra Thakur's Parallel Philosophy · Parallel Philosophy: constructive theses · Chapter 68

debates.proof: Parallel theology does not regard atheism as a moral vacuum, nor does it equate faith with superstition. Prudential pluralism means that different religious and non-religious views of life coexist with equal civic dignity, but the test of common propriety applies to public obligations. Religious freedom has at least three components: the right to profess one 's faith. the right to change one 's faith. the right to have no faith. Withdrawal from one of these three freedoms would be incomplete. The plurality of the intelligentsia sees religious life in three spheres. The first is the freedom to have a private conscience. Secondly, voluntary religious communities must be free and independent, with the right to membership and the opportunity to leave. Third, despite state laws, equal citizenship is paramount. The person can say that their religion forbids this practice and live their life accordingly. However, this is not enough to impose penal laws on all citizens. Public law should be such that even citizens with differing beliefs or distrusts can understand and examine its logic. Religion can mean community, compassion, service, discipline, art, memory, and hope. A sensible plurality would not deny this contribution. But religious institutions can also produce injustices of power, property, gender, caste or discipline. Respect is not freedom from criticism. The neutrality of the state is not heresy. Neutrality meant equal civil liberties for all religions and non-religion, without royal prerogative to any one spiritual truth. The state should protect dharma, which means freedom and security. not the domination of any religion. Pluralism does not say that all religious claims are equally true. Contradictory metaphysical claims cannot all be true in the same sense. Pluralistic politics does not mean abandoning truth-telling; it means rejecting violence, oppression or unequal citizenship in the face of dissent. Religious ideas and texts and institutions are subject to public criticism. Faith does not give the right to withhold criticism. But insulting individuals is not the same as collective blaming and violent intimidation. Distinctions should be judged by topic, language, goals, and strengths. Sharp sarcasm may be offensive; however, the law must limit direct harm. Religious communities could hold debates and peaceful protests in response. The answer to disagreement is not violence. The state is supposed to give equal protection. Marriage binds the individual to a continuum of life-determinations, family relationships and religious communities. Stay at an adult independent counseling center. Community disapproval is not a sufficient reason for legal prohibition. Let there be an impartial inquiry into the allegations of fraud or violence and not just suspicion due to different religion. The security and privacy of the couple are essential. The upbringing of the child is determined by ritual and inheritance communication. The state should not impose one religion rule but protect one uniform civil code. People deserve equal respect and opinions are not equal truths. It is the center of the plurality of differences. A person who holds a false opinion does not lose citizenship. Opinions should be judged by evidence, consistency, and ethical consequences. The idea that the safety of individuals is immutable has attracted criticism. It 's not possible to say you 're wrong about the communication, and that doesn 't diminish your authority. Truth-seeking and democratic equality are combined here. For common reasons, major religions or secular powers may declare their language to be universal. The concept of minority is weak in translation. So public reason is not a static dictionary; it is a process of mutual translation. Religious reasons must be presented, as well as the relationship between authority and shared experience. Power should not be decided unilaterally by what is acceptable. Publicity makes for open debate, judicial scrutiny, and equal opportunity to speak. In a free society, honest people will disagree on the ultimate religious question because the evidence, experience, and interpretation are complex. Plurality cannot be a temporary defect of ignorance alone.
debates.response: Truth-telling and civil rights are different levels I can disagree, argue, and change my beliefs about religious truths. However, the basis of civil rights should not depend on a decision about which religion is true. This division allows for truth-telling to survive and limits political repression.
debates.synthesis: The rational pluralism of religions combines three strands: freedom of conscience and public reason, and equal citizenship. It does not confine religion to a private chamber; it accepts its social life but defines the limits of state dominance.
debates.source: Gajendra Thakur's Parallel Philosophy · Parallel Philosophy: constructive theses · Chapter 69

debates.proof: History is not just a record of the victors. But simply telling the story of the hysteria does not make the story true. The purpose of the parallel historiography is not to create a new myth by reversing the main story; it is to widen the scope, identify silences, and apply the same critical criteria to all claims. The state, courts, institutions, and the educated class leave more than written records. Poor, women, workers, and rural communities may have less exposure to regional languages and oral traditions. Because of this inequality, the available resources themselves reflect social power. Why is there less of a group on record? The document has been destroyed. There was no means of writing it. The organization did not consider his experience to be important. Parallel histories treat silence as a question rather than a fact. The reason for the silence must be sought, not to fill the empty space with imagination. Personal letters, local documents, oral histories, songs, registers, archaeological objects, maps, newspapers, court records, economic data, women 's domestic writings, and regional language literature can all be useful, along with official records. However, the nature, date, purpose, transmission, and extent of each source should be specified. Official sources may be influenced by power, or folklore may also be adapted. Royal documents are not automatically true or oral stories are automatically true. The moral of parallel history is not to have soft evidence for your favorite stories. To understand history only in terms of kings, class only, religion only, caste only, language only or economy only may be incomplete. The causes of the many levels interact. The parallel historiography accepts a multifactorial interpretation of the evidence instead of a monolithic determinism. Regional histories do not aim to create mythical glory separate from national histories. Mithila 's local sources, language, registers, literature, folklore, and cross-border Nepal-India references can enrich the broader history. However, each claim will ask for sources and comparative evidence from the date. Regional self-esteem may be a motivator for historiography, not a substitute for evidence. The sincerity of the historian lies in making the level of inference clear. Explicit if there is strong evidence, probabilistic if partial, controversial if source-contradictory, anonymous if there is no evidence. Call conclusions that are outside the range of available evidence unlikely to be true. The findings influence when history is shared and for how long. Periods of dynastic change, economic change, or linguistic movement can vary. Convenient centimeters can cut out the actual process. The reason for the scheduling must be clear. Both continuity and break-up are to be seen across the border. Local time cannot correspond to the national time division. Multiple valid chronologies of the same event are possible but not arbitrary. The source and the purpose of the analysis will provide the basis. Intellectual history is not just a list of places of birth. The centres of learning, guru-shishya relationships, manuscript transmission, patronage, debate and migration shape the geography of knowledge. Some have called it a philosophical treatise on birth, work, tradition, or influence. The criterion should be clear, as in the text. Limitations are not arbitrary to promote pride. Mithila is made up of external dialogues. The movement of ideas explains their historical form without losing regional specificity. Digital copying simplifies searching by adding remote sources and enables new comparisons. However, incorrect text-reading and incomplete metadata and duplication of copies can give false certainty. Digital images do not capture the paper, ink, pattern, or margins of the original object perfectly. For important findings, basic or high-quality evidence should be examined. The choice of the database itself is epistemological. What collections are digitized, what is searchable, and who owns them is the new question of historiography. Regional pride can lead to selective storytelling, the stigmatization of outsiders, and mythological antiquity. The danger of this is real.
debates.response: Parallelism Expands the Field of Evidence If adding new sources changes the old conclusion, it is not a defeat of objectivity but an improvement. Objectivity is not the absence of a point of view but rather the availability of diverse sources, clear methods, and critical examination and revision.
debates.synthesis: The formula for parallel histories is read center, read margin, read silence. But apply the same logic to all. Parallelism is not an excuse to make assumptions; it is a responsibility to find evidence.
debates.source: Gajendra Thakur's Parallel Philosophy · Parallel Philosophy: constructive theses · Chapter 70

debates.objection: The Thirty Precepts do not constitute a strict code of ethics. The objection is a valid one. Aphorisms are mnemonic, so they run the risk of becoming harsh slogans. If only the sutras were repeated without context on each complex question, they would become aphorisms instead of philosophies.
debates.proof: To condense the long discourse of this text into thirty aphorisms is not an abstraction but the very essence of the philosophical discipline. The purpose of a sutra is not to make complex ideas into slogans but to provide mnemonic scales with which the reader can examine new questions, controversies, and the institution 's traditions and experiences. Each sutra is an independent sentence, but together they form an interconnected structure of parallel philosophies. 1. Truth can be multifaceted and not arbitrary. The first part of this thread assumes that complex realities can be seen as different from separate social, historical, linguistic, or empirical spaces. The second part makes clear that plurality of viewpoints is not arbitrary privatization of truth. Contradiction and proof: Objective resistance and public scrutiny are still necessary. 2. Knowledge is possible, but research is difficult. Human knowledge is neither omniscient nor meaningless. Conclusions can be accepted if the evidence is strong or modified if new evidence emerges. The absence of infallibility does not prove the impossibility of knowledge. For this reason, humility and intellectual courage are not mutually exclusive. 3. There are many types of proofs. each one has its proper field. Direct inferences, reliable linguistic statements, documents, scientific tests, statistical analysis, historical sources, oral memory, and self-experience are not the same kind of evidence. The value of the proof is determined by the nature of the question. Personal experience may be the basis of personal sense, but not the sufficiency of public law itself. 4. Defeating the opposition by making them weak is not an argument. The theory of strong antipartisans is the basic thesis of parallel philosophy. Offer opposing views only if their supporters agree with them. And then there are the criticisms. Making a false impression to win can be rude or sarcastic, not fact-finding. 5. Tradition is evidence that an idea is old; it is not proof that the idea is right. Long-term traditions can provide memories and social continuity. But age is not a moral legitimacy. Racial slurs, gender inequality, or violence are simply not acceptable in the long run. To question tradition respectfully is to test its morality rather than destroy it. 6. Innovation is proof that an idea is new. not proof that the idea is superior. Modernity is not superior to science or technology or a new political language simply because it is new. New systems can also lead to exploitation, surveillance, environmental destruction, or inequality. The criterion of progress is not novelty but dignity, freedom, justice, truthfulness and impact on life. 7. Birth is not a moral qualification. Caste, clan, lineage, gender, religion, language, region, or family status does not make a person morally high or low. Birth is a fact of circumstance, not a moral attribute. This thread challenges both the claims of hereditary privilege and social inferiority. 8. The dignity of a human being precedes social status. The value of a person is not derived from position, wealth, education, caste, religion or state titles. Social norms may reinforce or offend basic human values, but they must be respected. For this reason, denigration, dehumanization, and instrumentalization are morally wrong. 9. Freedom without equality can become the privilege of the powerful. Mere formal freedom is not enough if the resources, education, security, social respect and opportunities are so unequal that only a few can make use of the freedom. Here equality cannot be the enemy of liberty but its real social condition. 10. Freedom without equality can lead to control. Equality can be oppressive if the individual 's freedom of conscience, choice, belief, way of life and expression is taken away in the name of making everyone equal. Equality is the same human-standard, not mechanical uniformity. 11. Liberty and equality without fraternity are difficult to sustain in social life.
debates.response: The thread is not a judgment, it is a question. These formulas are used to guide the question rather than to provide a ready answer. Technical competence may not be morally permissible, but whether a particular technique is appropriate may require separate evidence, risk, benefits, and rights analysis. Birth does not confer moral merit but does require additional arguments on the proper form of social policy. So the thread opens the door and does not close the discussion.
debates.synthesis: The threads of parallel philosophies combine truth and proof, dignity and freedom and equality, religion and state, science and language, history and compassion, and introspection into a single critical discipline. Its central tenet is that no source, institution, tradition, majority, marginalization, technology or philosophy itself is the private master of truth and morality. Ask for proof, identify limitations, listen to the opposition, maintain decorum, and be open to amending your conclusions.
debates.source: Gajendra Thakur's Parallel Philosophy · Parallel Philosophy: constructive theses · Chapter 71

debates.objection: Wouldn 't such open-mindedness be without judgment? Observing introspection and pluralism may lead to the objection that parallel philosophies leave every question open-ended. If everyone is inventive, how can one make strong ethical decisions?
debates.proof: Parallelism is not just about opposing the mainstream. In parallel, the text contains more method names than place names. It refers to the intellectual state where established knowledge is respectfully examined, neglected sources are discovered, the same critical criteria apply to both, and the conclusions themselves are open to revision. The first chapter of the text considered darsanas to be a self-conscious act of asking for reasons rather than a collection of answers. Even in the last chapter, this does not change. The difference is that now the detailed geography of the question has been looked at: science and reality, Indian philosophy and Mithila, Western philosophy and society, state and religion, modernity and the digital world, artificial intelligence and environment and history. This journey leads to a conclusion: the question is not only of doubt. it is also of responsibility. If I question authority, I will question the authority of my party. If you ask for proof of tradition, then so be it on the claim of modernity. If you look for silences in official histories, so do the fact-checks in Hashiya 's stories. Parallelism is the discipline of symmetric criticism. The text does not aim to make Mithila a new center of world philosophy. Such a claim would be against the polycentric spirit of parallel philosophy. Mithila is here a place of systematic recollection, a place of dialogue with the Upanishadic questions of jurisprudence, the logic and discipline of jurisprudence, the nuances of word and evidence, the traditions of scripture, the experiences of public life, and modern social questions. Mithali 's contribution may be a matter of pride but pride is not a substitute for proof. For this reason, acknowledging uncertainties in historical claims as uncertainties has been part of the text 's method of not writing down traditional stories as historical facts and not forcing modern concepts onto the past. Studies of Indian philosophy show that these Indian schools of thought are not uniform traditions. Sāṅkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mīmāṃsā, Vedanta, Buddhism, Jainism, and the Lokayatas have serious disagreements on jñāna, ātman, Ishvara, matter, language, karma, moksha, and pramana. In this disagreement, intellectual life is not the weakness of Indian philosophy. The Upanishads teach questions. the discipline of just proof. the subtleties of Mīmāṃsā language and method. Buddhist philosophy. the critique of suffering and impermanence and self-imagination. the discipline of the Jain philosophical approach. the challenge of locative doubt. Parallel philosophies do not dissolve these in an artificial Indian belief system. The Greek question, medieval logic, modern rationalism-empiricism, Kant 's criticism, Hegel 's history-view, Marx 's structure-analysis, the individual responsibility of existentialism, the clarity of analytic philosophy, the exploration of pragmatism and the methodology of science-philosophy are all independent voices in parallel discourse. The purpose of the comparison is not to prove that an Indian philosopher had already stated modern Western theories or that all Western ideas are repetitions of Indian sources. Such a triumphalistic comparison destroys the historical distinctiveness of both traditions. Meaningful comparison occurs at the level of the problem, argument, and objection. Caste, class, gender, language, region, state, liberty, equality, justice and democracy are not merely subjects of sociology. Within these questions are the core philosophical questions of human value, rights and legality, responsibility and identity, and institutional propriety. Gandhi raises the ethical questions of non-violence and Swaraj, the relationship between means. Ambedkar brings out the inseparable relationship between caste, dignity, representation, constitutionality and liberty-equality-bondage. Parallel philosophy does not eliminate the differences between the two, but rather puts them into concrete moral testing.
debates.response: Openness and Moral Boundaries Are Simultaneously Possible Modification does not have to make everything uncertain. Some moral boundaries may be clear enough: birth is not a moral qualification. a person is not just a means. unnecessary suffering is not appropriate. the state is not the master of the citizen. religious freedom is also a freedom of conscience. majority is not proof of truth. technical competence is not a moral sanction. The application of these limitations may be controversial, but the controversy is not without moral ambiguities. The Final Conclusion Parallel philosophy is not an end in itself. If this text declares itself complete on its last page, it would violate its last aphorism. The future of philosophy lies not in closed systems, but in better questions, new evidence, more inclusive dialogue, and a more just life. In this sense, to be parallel is not to be marginalized. one is not enslaved to a single center in the search for truth. The combined exercise of freedom of question, the discipline of proof, the ethics of dignity, the critique of authority, the wisdom of pluralism, and the courage of introspection are the living embodiments of a parallel philosophy.
debates.source: Gajendra Thakur's Parallel Philosophy · Parallel Philosophy: constructive theses · Chapter 72
